mechanism_narrative: Consistently low federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS < 3.0%) compress discount rates applied to equity cash flows, increasing present value of future earnings and producing positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 3.0% (t-test p > 0.05 vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Annualized CPI inflation exceeding 3.0% (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY) triggers central bank rate hikes that increase equity discount rates, reducing present value of future cash flows and causing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annualized).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strong employment growth (PAYEMS > 0.5% MoM) and low unemployment (UNRATE < 5.0%) signal robust consumer spending power that boosts corporate earnings, driving positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The joint condition (PAYEMS > 0.5% MoM and UNRATE < 5.0%) occurs but 5-day returns are negative in > 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle regimes (FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY), declining housing starts (HOUST < 2150) indicate overbuilding and reduced consumer spending, causing negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances where HOUST < 2150 during late-cycle regimes (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, CPIAUCSL > 3.0%).

mechanism_narrative: Declining housing starts (HOUST < 2150) signal weak consumer demand for dwellings, reducing construction sector revenue and corporate earnings growth, producing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: HOUST < 2150 but 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production falling below 95.0 (INDPRO < 95.0) indicates manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output and profit margins, causing negative 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 95.0 but 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising > 0.25% per month), higher short-term rates increase equity discount rates and reduce risk appetite, causing negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS rising > 0.25% per month but 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous weak housing demand (HOUST < 2150) and weak industrial output (INDPRO < 100) indicate broad economic contraction that reduces corporate revenue growth, triggering negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The joint condition (HOUST < 2150 and INDPRO < 100) occurs but 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of cases.
